# survalis <img src="man/figures/logo.svg" align="right" height="139" alt="survalis logo" />

Unified survival machine learning and interpretability in R.

<!-- badges: start -->
[![CRAN status](https://www.r-pkg.org/badges/version/survalis)](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=survalis)
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/ielbadisy/survalis/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/ielbadisy/survalis/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![CRAN downloads](https://cranlogs.r-pkg.org/badges/grand-total/survalis)](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=survalis)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT)
<!-- badges: end -->

`survalis` provides a unified framework for survival machine learning in R.
Seven verbs cover the whole workflow for 22 built-in learners and for any
learner you write yourself: fitting, prediction, resampled and external
evaluation, tuning, paired comparison, model-agnostic interpretation, and
causal contrasts.

`survalis` is available on CRAN: <https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=survalis>.

## The seven-verb interface

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(survalis)
f <- Surv(time, status) ~ age + karno + celltype

m   <- fit(f, veteran, model = "ranger", spec = list(num.trees = 500))
predict(m, veteran[1:5, ], times = c(90, 180, 365))          # survival matrix
evaluate(m, times = c(90, 180, 365), resampling = cv(5))     # resampled metrics

cmp <- compare(f, veteran, models = c("coxph", "ranger", "densemlp"),
               times = c(90, 180, 365))
plot(cmp)

plot(interpret(m, "shap", newdata = veteran[1, ], times = 180))
estimate(f, veteran, model = "ranger", treatment = "trt", tau = 365)
```

`fit()`, `predict()`, `evaluate()`, `tune()`, `compare()`, `interpret()` and
`estimate()` are the whole interface. Resampling is described by `cv()`,
`holdout()`, `group_cv()` and `bootstrap()`, and `list_survlearners()`,
`list_metrics()` and `list_interpretability_methods()` give the valid ids.
Upgrading from 1.x? See `vignette("from-1.0", package = "survalis")`.



## Installation

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# Install the released version from CRAN
install.packages("survalis")

# Or install the development version from GitHub
remotes::install_github("ielbadisy/survalis")
```



## Core philosophy

* Seven verbs cover the whole workflow: `fit()`, `predict()`, `evaluate()`, `tune()`, `compare()`, `interpret()`, `estimate()`
* One function per job: learners are chosen by `model`, metrics by `metrics`, explanations by `method`, outputs by `type`
* Every verb returns an S3 object with `print()`, `summary()`, `plot()` and `as.data.frame()` methods
* Matrix predictions are survival matrices: one row per subject, columns `t=100`, `t=200`, ..., with the grid recorded in `attr(x, "times")`
* A custom learner is two functions, `list(fit = , predict = )`, and works with every verb



## Exploring the package

```{r}
library(survalis)
list_survlearners()               # ids for `model`
list_metrics()                    # ids for `metrics`
list_interpretability_methods()   # ids for `method` in interpret()
```



## Basic Workflow

**1. Fit a model**
```{r}
mod_cox <- fit(Surv(time, status) ~ age + karno + celltype, veteran, model = "coxph")
mod_cox
```


**2. Predict survival probabilities**

```{r}
pred <- predict(mod_cox, newdata = veteran[1:5, ], times = c(100, 200))
pred
```

`predict()` also returns other quantities via `type`: `"risk"` (1 - S(t)),
`"chf"`, `"hazard"`, `"rmst"`, `"quantile"`, `"median"`.


**3. Evaluate model performance**

```{r}
ev <- evaluate(mod_cox, times = c(80, 160), resampling = cv(5, seed = 123))
ev
```

```{r}
summary(ev)
```

To score a model on data it was not trained on, pass `newdata`; to score
predictions made elsewhere, pass the survival matrix and the outcome.

```{r}
train <- veteran[1:100, ]
test  <- veteran[-(1:100), ]
m_tr  <- fit(Surv(time, status) ~ age + karno + celltype, train, model = "coxph")
evaluate(m_tr, newdata = test, times = c(80, 160))

S <- predict(m_tr, test, times = c(80, 160))
evaluate(S, y = Surv(test$time, test$status))
```


**4. Compare multiple learners**

`compare()` evaluates every learner on the *same* resampling folds, so results
are paired; `tune = TRUE` tunes each tunable learner first.

```{r}
cmp <- compare(
  Surv(time, status) ~ age + karno + celltype,
  data = veteran,
  models = c("coxph", "rpart", "ranger"),
  times = c(80, 160),
  resampling = cv(3, seed = 1)
  )

cmp
plot(cmp)
```



**5. Bring your own learner**

A custom learner is a list with a `fit` function and a `predict` function that
returns one row per subject and one column per time. It then works with every
verb.

```{r}
expo <- list(
  name = "exponential",
  fit = function(formula, data, ...) survival::survreg(formula, data, dist = "exponential"),
  predict = function(object, newdata, times) {
    rate <- 1 / predict(object, newdata, type = "response")
    exp(-outer(rate, times))
  }
)

compare(Surv(time, status) ~ age + karno + celltype, veteran,
        models = list("coxph", expo), times = c(80, 160),
        resampling = cv(3, seed = 1))
```



**6. Visualize interpretation**

`interpret()` is the single entry point to every explanation method, and
`plot()` draws its result.

```{r}
shap_meanabs <- interpret(
  mod_cox, "shap",
  newdata     = veteran[100, ],
  times       = 80,
  sample.size = 50,
  aggregate   = TRUE,
  shap_method = "meanabs"
  )

as.data.frame(shap_meanabs)
```

```{r}
plot(shap_meanabs)
```

### More interpretability methods

`survalis` also provides PDP, ALE, surrogate explanations, tree surrogates,
permutation importance, interaction analysis, and counterfactuals, all
through `interpret(fit, method = ..., ...)`.

**Partial dependence and ICE**

```{r}
pdp_age <- interpret(mod_cox, "pdp", feature = "age", times = c(100, 200, 300))

plot(pdp_age, which = "per_time")
plot(pdp_age, which = "integrated", smooth = TRUE)
```

**Accumulated local effects**

```{r}
ale_karno <- interpret(mod_cox, "ale", feature = "karno", times = c(100, 200, 300))

plot(ale_karno, which = "per_time")
plot(ale_karno, which = "integrated", smooth = TRUE)
```

**Local surrogate explanation**

```{r}
local_surrogate <- interpret(
  mod_cox, "surrogate",
  newdata     = veteran[1, , drop = FALSE],
  times       = c(100, 200, 300),
  target_time = 200,
  k           = 5
  )

as.data.frame(local_surrogate)
plot(local_surrogate, top_n = 10)
```

**Tree surrogate**

```{r}
tree_surrogate <- interpret(mod_cox, "tree_surrogate", times = c(100, 200, 300))

plot(tree_surrogate, type = "importance", top_n = 5)
# plot(tree_surrogate, type = "tree")
```

**Permutation variable importance**

```{r}
varimp_res <- interpret(
  mod_cox, "varimp",
  times          = c(100, 200, 300),
  metric         = "ibs",
  n_repetitions  = 5,
  seed           = 123
  )

as.data.frame(varimp_res)
plot(varimp_res)
```

**Feature interactions**

```{r}
interaction_1way <- interpret(mod_cox, "interaction", times = c(100, 200, 300),
                              target_time = 200, type = "1way")
interaction_heatmap <- interpret(mod_cox, "interaction", times = c(100, 200, 300),
                                 target_time = 200, type = "heatmap")
interaction_time <- interpret(mod_cox, "interaction", times = c(100, 200, 300),
                              type = "time")

plot(interaction_1way, type = "1way")
plot(interaction_heatmap, type = "heatmap")
plot(interaction_time, type = "time")
```

**Counterfactual explanations**

```{r}
counterfactuals <- interpret(
  mod_cox, "counterfactual",
  newdata            = veteran[1, , drop = FALSE],
  times              = c(100, 200, 300),
  target_time        = 200,
  features_to_change = c("age", "karno", "diagtime"),
  cost_penalty       = 0.01
  )

as.data.frame(counterfactuals)
```

**7. Calibration, ROC and decision curves**

```{r}
interpret(mod_cox, "calibration", eval_time = 80, n_bins = 10, n_boot = 30) |> plot()
interpret(m_tr, "roc", newdata = test, eval_time = 80) |> plot()
interpret(m_tr, "dca", newdata = test, eval_time = 80) |> plot()
```
